title: Fragment — On the Dead and Their Persistence

pages.text:
The dead do not go. This is not a matter of theology — it is a matter of physics, which is to say it is a matter of resonance, which is to say it is a matter of what the stone remembers.

When a body ceases, the accumulated resonance in its bone does not cease with it. Resonance is not a property of the living. It is a property of the stone of the body, which is the same as the stone of the ground, which is the same as the stone of the walls, which is the same as the stone the bell was made to address. The dead are not elsewhere. The dead are precisely here, in the frequency of the grey stone, indistinguishable from every other thing the stone has ever held.

The student asketh: then how do we speak to the dead?

The teacher answereth: thou already dost. Every time thou standest near the grey stone and feelest nothing, thou art in the presence of everyone who hath ever stood there. Thou art not feeling nothing. Thou art feeling everything, which is the same as nothing, to a mind that cannot distinguish.
